primary.justification: The chapter's entire structure is built around explaining climate as a key natural phenomenon — its types across India, its determinants (latitude, altitude, proximity to sea, winds, topography), the monsoon mechanism, climate-linked disasters, and climate change. Every named section develops some aspect of explaining climate as a natural phenomenon. Without it the chapter has no purpose.

The chapter contains a dedicated, self-contained section 'Climate Change' that analyses human-caused global warming, India's rising temperatures, and evaluates specific mitigation measures (renewable energy, tree planting, energy efficiency, sustainable lifestyles) including their tension with economic growth goals — directly meeting C-6.3's demand to analyse Indian perspectives and efforts towards conservation in the context of global climate change. This section could be taught as a lesson in its own right.

The chapter contains a dedicated section 'Climate and our Lives' that directly correlates climate with patterns of livelihoods — wheat cultivation in northern plains, rice and spices on the western coast, and the socioeconomic consequences of monsoon failure (agricultural disruption, food price rises, migration of agricultural labourers, industrial dependence on water). This section is self-contained and devoted to the livelihood–climate correlation that C-6.4 demands.

The chapter identifies regional patterns of agricultural suitability across geographies — the wet western coast for rice and spices, the northern plains for wheat, the Deccan as semi-arid. These appear as illustrations within climate-type descriptions rather than a dedicated resource-distribution section, so it is present but not a main focus.

IMD's colour-coded warning system is described in detail in the weather prediction subsection, and the NDRF's role is mentioned under Cyclones. Institutions appear in named passages about disaster response, but only in passing rather than as a developed theme.
